supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40:07 UTC, WS-ARUIZ-01 connected to DC-PIN-01 over SMB on port 445. The DC recorded a network logon and logoff for the WS-ARUIZ-01$ machine account. These records do not identify a share, file, or process associated with the connection.
At 13:40:04 UTC, the DC recorded Kerberos activity for the WS-ARUIZ-01$ machine account, including a service ticket for DC-PIN-01$.

At 14:02 UTC, the DC recorded a Kerberos service ticket for raj.patel to WS-ARUIZ-01. This establishes ticket activity after the reported window of the brief PowerShell appearance, but does not establish a remote session or connect that activity to the alert.

The available endpoint process records after the collection outage show conhost.exe running as SYSTEM, launched by csrss.exe at 14:17 and ending at 14:19; these records do not identify a PowerShell process.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied coverage status reports that WS-ARUIZ-01 winsec and Sysmon logs were not collected from 13:20 through 14:15 UTC because of a collection outage. This overlaps the reported PowerShell appearance and leaves the endpoint process and command-line evidence for that period unavailable.

The network records identify connections and authentication activity, but the provided records do not show which process initiated the 13:40 SMB connection or what share or files, if any, were accessed.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually ran on WS-ARUIZ-01 around 13:40 UTC, and if so, its command line, script content, parent process, and user context.
Whether the 13:40 SMB and Kerberos activity was related to the reported PowerShell window or to authorized work.
Whether the later raj.patel ticket activity resulted in a remote session or any action on WS-ARUIZ-01.
Whether the alerted activity was malicious or benign.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain endpoint EDR, PowerShell, process-creation, and interactive-session telemetry for WS-ARUIZ-01 from 13:20 to 14:15 UTC, including process ancestry, command lines, script-block or transcription logs, and relevant file activity.
Review DC-PIN-01 and FILE-PIN-01 SMB, authentication, and file-access records around 13:40 UTC to determine the purpose and account context of the workstation's activity.
Confirm with Ana Ruiz and IT whether any PowerShell use or remote maintenance was expected around 13:40 UTC, and whether the later raj.patel ticket activity was authorized.
unrelated_findings: WS-ARUIZ-01 had TLS connections to WS-TWEBER-01 on port 443 at 13:33 UTC. The supplied records do not identify the application or purpose; review separately if this is not an expected internal service. (T064-00085, T064-00086, T064-00088, T064-00090)

At 14:06 UTC, the DC recorded NTLM validation for ana.ruiz with workstation DC-PIN-01, and WS-RPATEL-01 recorded a type 3 NTLM logon for ana.ruiz from the DC's IP address. The records do not explain this authentication path; review separately and do not treat it as evidence deciding this alert. (T064-00242, T064-00243)
